cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Try It First
cards.instruction: Get someone else to test the shortcut, substitute, or questionable fix before you rely on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Taste this coffee substitute before I fill my cup. A small sip, please; we're assessing flavour, not thirst.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We have proper coffee. Why should I spoil breakfast?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A sample is not a serving. One spoonful, then water to clear your palate; I'll make proper coffee if it fails.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You take the spoonful. Your cup's empty too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I need an unprompted reaction. If I taste first, I'll influence yours. One spoonful, please, before you add any sugar.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 sample size, A3 palate control and A5 unprompted-reaction claim make professional testing the reason B must try the substitute first.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 breakfast concern causes A3 minimal sample and fallback; B4 role swap causes A5 claimed observer influence.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants normal breakfast and B4 fairly suggests A take the risk, forcing A to justify the asymmetry.

heightening.evidence: A5 recasts B4 first-taste request as a threat to test quality and renews B task.

specificity.evidence: A1 substitute before A filled cup and B4 both empty cups establish the personal-use sequence.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 tasting-order explanation is directly addressed to B role challenge, not added history or an external reviewer.
